sermon.title: The Seventh Seal — Book of Revelation
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Continuing in Revelation, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches the seventh seal and the first six trumpets (Revelation 8-10), arguing the visions are not a chronological timeline and that the saints are still on earth, praying, sealed and protected. He stresses the power of the prayers of the saints, God’s delay so more can repent, and a glorious church preaching the gospel right up to Christ’s coming.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: the captions read “first ionians 5:4,” rendered 1 Thessalonians 5:4, and “Luke 188,” rendered Luke 18:8. He corrects himself from “First Thessalonians” to 1 Timothy 2:4. His figures for the earth’s salt water, fresh water and land, his statement about the distance of the nearest star, his placing of the stable in Jerusalem, and his comments about named wealthy people, end-time authors and Bible translations are his own and are not verified here. A few words are marked [unclear].

faqs.question: How long was the silence in heaven at the seventh seal?
faqs.answer: He says there was silence in heaven for half an hour, and jokes that “most of us have been silent all of our life let alone a half an hour.”

faqs.question: Will 144,000 Jewish virgins evangelize the world in the tribulation?
faqs.answer: He says that teaching “is pure fantasy.”

faqs.question: Is there any other way to be made righteous?
faqs.answer: He says no; we are given white robes of righteousness because of the blood Jesus shed, and “there is no other way it’s him.”

faqs.question: Is the word “rapture” in the Bible?
faqs.answer: He says “there’s no word rapture in the Bible”; they are talking about First Thessalonians where it says we’re caught up.

faqs.question: Does praying in your closet mean praying silently?
faqs.answer: He says the closet means your attitude; we know the prayers of Jesus and David because they prayed out loud.

faqs.question: What does he say faith is?
faqs.answer: He says “faith is doing something because you don’t have it but you know it’s there,” because you know it’s the right thing to do.

faqs.question: What does he say about how much fresh water the earth has?
faqs.answer: He gives his figures for salt water, fresh water and land, and asks whether people could live with a little less fresh water: “Not that big a difference is there.”

faqs.question: Are the horses with lion heads literal?
faqs.answer: He says it is “just an illustration so we can understand the vastness of it and the power of it.”

faqs.question: Which Bible translation does he prefer?
faqs.answer: He says the King James is his favorite Bible for study because it has very few misguided translations, though he reads other versions and warns about errors in some.

faqs.question: Is the church on defense or offense against hell?
faqs.answer: He says the gates of hell are on the defense: “we’re on the offense man we’re beating them back.”

faqs.question: Why must believers eat the whole book?
faqs.answer: He says until the word gets into the belly it isn’t broken down to nourish your spiritual man; “the whole book is what’s going to make the difference in your home.”

faqs.question: Who does he call the eleventh virgin?
faqs.answer: He says someone was out there saying “the bridegroom cometh”; that wise, awake one with oil that lasts “that’s the church of the living God.”

faqs.question: What if Jesus doesn’t come back for a thousand years?
faqs.answer: He says we can still have what He promised now, and theory people “always” come up with a fresh book to cover up yesterday’s mistakes.
